severity-narrowed-to-the-dictionary-thre.why: THE DECLARED DIVERGENCE'S OWN JUSTIFICATION, in the one form that can fail. The owner decided `IncidentReport.severity` keeps FOUR values against PRIV-SRS-02's three, and the whole reason is that `critical` is the only value carrying a containment deadline - so narrowing the list would retire the only containment target in the module as a side effect of a type change. Planted, it kills THREE tests, two of them the ones that carry the reason: 'no member of INCIDENT_SEVERITIES other than `critical` carries a target' and 'removing `critical` would leave the module with NO containment target at all'. Written as prose this reason is a sentence somebody deletes; written as these tests it is a red build. The record is `docs/pcms-dictionary-divergences.md` section 1.

containment-stamp-without-an-action.why: Her first sentence, «لما أضغط ع زر الاحتواء بس بغيّر الحالة إلى تم احتوائه», in the one place it can come back. Planted, the status stamp would be written with an EMPTY log - which is exactly the state she pressed - and it kills the unit test named after her words plus the ordering test beside it. Against a real database it ALSO fails at the trigger `IncidentReport_contained_needs_an_action`, which is the half that survives any later code path: the defect is unrepresentable rather than merely refused here.
